meaning: the entity is one movement of one carrier state, such as a stock tote or a closed order, from one flow node to another
_notes: `owner` is `agent-studio`, who answers for this shape today; the registry moves ownership freely (world-proto server/DESIGN.md section 7). Lead decided, say if not.

The schema is open to fields it does not name, as every registry schema is (world-proto SPEC section 9's lenient reading), so a misspelt optional field passes WPS and is carried unread. Lead decided, say if not.

A reference field takes a declared or derived identity, bare or with any pin, as the core's references do (without their `local_ref`); the pin rule, enforced on world-proto master since c384e59, refuses a wrong pin in its own sentence, and `refs[].pin` says which pin each field takes. Lead decided, say if not.
An optional list, when present, holds at least one entry, so an empty list never says something different from an absent one. Lead decided, say if not.
`when.container`, `when.exit_path` and `when.routing` are lists: "any of" read as the values the guard admits. Lead decided, say if not.

`storage_fallback` is left out: the flow spec defers it (section 10), and its sector lists inside a list need the annotation `/storage_fallback/*/*`, which WPS's extractor cannot follow before complete annotation traversal lands (world-proto server/DESIGN.md section 16, phase 7).

Not in the schema, the flow compiler's to check: `returns_by` only on edges from stations into storage; `storage_scope` only at a storage end, naming that node's own sectors; an alternative sharing its primary's `to` and `moves`; `phase` only on leftover edges.

schema.title: flow.material_edge
schema.description: the entity is one movement of one carrier state, such as a stock tote or a closed order, from one flow node to another
schema.$comment: Written for world-proto's registry from Agent Studio's 06-flow-panel-and-compiler.md section 3.1 (notes/agent-studio-2026-10-17/design/specs/06-flow-panel-and-compiler.md). Open to fields a newer writer adds (SPEC section 9).

from.description: The node the carrier starts at.

to.description: The node the carrier ends at.

moves.description: What moves: `units`, product without a modelled carrier, or a carrier state.

alternative_to.description: An edge this one competes with to bring the same carrier state to the same node; the destination chooses per opening, in scheduler time.

bias.description: The handicap in that choice: `fleet_pressure`, derived from the map, or a fixed signed simtime, positive favouring this edge.

opens_at_sim_ms.description: No task starts on this edge before this simtime.

until_sim_ms.description: No task starts on this edge from this simtime on.

storage_scope.description: At a storage end: which of the storage node's sectors this edge may use; absent, all of them.

returns_by.description: The return rule this edge shares with the other return edges its root serves.

guard.title: guard
guard.description: Which carriers take this edge: on `order:closed` edges the containers, exit paths and routings it admits; `phase` on leftover edges. An absent field admits all.

routing.description: The workload's designations this edge admits.

induction.title: induction
induction.description: How inbound units are inducted, on a `units` edge.

hour_gate.description: A lot waits for its hour.

units_per_tote.description: How many units fill one inbound tote; never the stored totes' fill, which is the scenario's.

reference.title: reference
reference.description: Another entity, by identity: a declared UUID or a derivation address, bare or with a pin. Which pin a field takes is the pin rule's to enforce: within the referrer's unit bare or `@head`, across units a changeset (a tag once tags land).

entity_id.title: entity id
entity_id.description: A declared entity's UUID or a derived entity's address, either arm (SPEC section 3).
